clue.text: Pages one might turn over before index, possibly?

definitions.text: Pages one might turn over before index, possibly?

parts.words: Pages one might turn over before index, possibly?
parts.note: read as a description of a book's back matter: the supplementary section a reader leafs through just before reaching the index

explanation.surface: A reader wonders which pages they might flick past on the way to the index.
explanation.definitionFit: In many books the supplementary matter at the back sits immediately ahead of the index.

clue.text: A vehicle carrying a hundred? You can count on it!

indicators.note: the vehicle holds the other pieces within it, as a bus carries passengers

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A bus loaded with a hundred passengers, and a jokey assurance that it is reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead frame is a counting device, so you literally count on it.

clue.text: Snoop grabbing insect in food store

indicators.note: the snooping word seizes the insect and holds it inside

parts.note: to snoop is to pry
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A nosy person catches an ant while poking around the larder.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder or cupboard for keeping provisions is a classic household food store.

clue.text: The admiral in the hold

definitions.meaning: Horatio, Britain's most famous naval commander, victor at Trafalgar
a wrestling grip applied from behind with the arms under the opponent's

explanation.walkthrough: A full or half version of this wrestling grip is named after the admiral; 'in' just joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Trafalgar hero and to a well-known wrestling grip.

clue.text: Policemen making censor spit

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers turn a censor into someone who spits.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors are a rank of police officer, so the plural names policemen.

clue.text: Dual nationality that's applicable to furniture

definitions.meaning: two nationalities side by side, one from France and one from Poland
a shellac finish rubbed onto wooden furniture to give a high gloss

explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link. The answer is two nationalities read separately, and as one phrase a traditional wood finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The two nationality words together name a glossy shellac finish applied to wooden furniture.

clue.text: Turn right, not having initial pint of draught

indicators.note: the drink word goes without the piece named, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a potation is a drink or draught

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone turns right after giving up the first pint of draught beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' removes P, the first letter of 'pint', from POTATION, a formal word for a drink, leaving OTATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotation is a turn, as of a wheel about its axis.

clue.text: Oscar's in trouble as a result of taking drugs

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and thrown into disorder

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Oscar has got into a mess because he took drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'S of 'Oscar's' counts here: OSCARS plus IN gives the eight letters; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor or unconsciousness caused by a narcotic is the medical result of taking drugs.

clue.text: Moving rapidly injured fish

parts.note: injured means hurt
a ling is a food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A wounded fish is moving fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle is to rush violently, so the participle means moving rapidly.

clue.text: Girl with catalogue for record producer

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A girl and a catalogue team up to make a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler writes annals, yearly records of events, so is a producer of records.

clue.text: One who looks hard for Sartre novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the name is given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone peers intently in search of a book by the French existentialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gazes fixedly is one who looks hard at something.

clue.text: Terribly dour poet dragged out of bed

indicators.note: the letters are treated terribly, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grumpy poet hauled from his bed in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not one for sleeping in.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant pulled up from its garden plot by the roots has been dragged out of its bed.

clue.text: Street register may be constitutional

parts.note: a roll is an official register or list

explanation.surface: A register of a street's residents might be a constitutional document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is a link; 'constitutional' is the noun, a walk taken for one's health.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a short walk taken for health, which is a leisurely amble.

clue.text: Spaniard and Thai, for example, going round Lake Superior

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the nationality word circles the other letters

parts.note: a Thai is an example of an Asian
U stands for upper class or superior

explanation.surface: A Spaniard and a Thai sail around one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake Superior' looks like the Great Lake but splits into L and U, the latter being the old British label for upper-class or superior usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Andalusia, the southern region of Spain, is a Spaniard.

clue.text: Loud-mouthed one starting endless agitation

indicators.note: agitation stirs things up, so the letters are shaken into a new order
the word starting loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A loudmouth is the one who stirs up endless trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts STARTING to STARTIN; with ONE that gives ten letters for 'agitation' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the loud-voiced herald Stentor in the Iliad, the adjective means extremely loud.

clue.text: Hitch-hiker's request for a tonic?

definitions.meaning: a hitch-hiker asks a passing driver to give them a lift
a drink or medicine that revives and refreshes

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a plea for a lift and an everyday term for a restorative drink.

clue.text: Set me up with crackers and cheese

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: crackers means mad, mental

explanation.surface: Someone lays out a plate of crackers and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' and 'with' are links; 'up' reverses ME to EM. 'crackers' is not biscuits but slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss cheese with large holes.

clue.text: They measure current time and energy invested in Cockney team

indicators.note: the two pieces are put inside the team's name

parts.note: West Ham United are the Hammers; a Cockney drops the H
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Time and energy put into a London football side.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop their H's; West Ham is an East London football club nicknamed the Hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter is an instrument that measures electric current in amperes.

clue.text: Tennyson's work: "At Home by Myself", "The Onset of Merlin" or "One in the Morning"

parts.note: at home means in
myself, the speaker, gives me

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A list of imaginary alternative titles for one of Tennyson's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. Each mock title gives pieces in turn, including M from the first letter of 'Merlin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's long elegy for his friend Arthur Hallam carries this Latin title.

clue.text: Deposit a couple of sailors

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the sailor word appears twice

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Two seamen put down a deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartar is the hard deposit that forms on teeth, also a crust left in wine casks.

clue.text: Dweeb wearing jacket?

parts.note: a dweeb is a fool or jerk
in means wearing, as in a person in a coat

explanation.surface: A nerd asks whether he should put on a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a sleeveless close-fitting jacket, often of leather.

clue.text: A hundred change sides immediately

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hundred people all switch sides at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change sides' looks like defecting, but 'sides' takes the first and last letters of 'change'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without delay, a direct synonym for immediately.

clue.text: Eager little boy wailed piteously

parts.note: eager means keen
Ed is a short form of Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic little boy cried pitifully.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to lament the dead with a wailing cry, so the past tense means wailed piteously.

clue.text: Dissident leader meeting primates -but outside capital

indicators.note: the word but sits on the outside, around the other pieces
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: apes are primates

explanation.surface: A rebel chief meets some apes, but somewhere beyond the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' is only a link; 'but' looks like a conjunction in the surface, yet its letters are the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary.

clue.text: Biblical character in Ecclesiastes the Rechabite

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A figure from the Bible appears in a book of scripture alongside a member of an ancient sect.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'Ecclesiastes', 'the' and the first letter of 'Rechabite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is the Jewish queen of Persia whose story is told in the Old Testament book named after her.

clue.text: Dicky, Stan and Mike may be wrong

indicators.note: dicky means unsound or shaky, so the letters are unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Three men, Dicky, Stan and Mike, could all be in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' poses as a third man's name but is the anagram signal; 'and' joins the fodder and 'may be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in error or holding a false belief is being wrong.

clue.text: See 5
Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: to fill with delight or put under a spell, a verb stressed on the second syllable
a door or opening by which a person goes inside

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt the same, the verb means to delight or bewitch and the noun means a doorway.
